citation.title: Cluster-Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data

standing_assumptions:
The article is Aronow, Samii and Assenova, ‘Cluster–Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data’, Political Analysis 23:564–577 (2015). Printed page = PDF page + 563 (printed p. 566 is PDF p. 3). Everything quoted below and in the targets was read from the rendered page images (staged/pages/p-NN.png, checked against 200–300 dpi renderings of staged/main.pdf). Primes are transposes. The paper writes $\epsilon_d$ for the population residual and $e_d$ for the fitted (sample) residual; the two are different objects throughout.
(S1) Sampling and dyads, p. 566 (PDF p. 3): “Begin with a large population from which we take a random (i.i.d.) sample of units, with the sample members indexed by $i = 1, ..., N$ and grouped into $D = \binom{N}{2} = N(N-1)/2$ dyads. Pairs of unit indices within each dyad map to dyadic indices, $1, ..., D$, through the index function $d(i,j) = d(j,i)$, with an inverse correspondence $s(d(i,j)) = \{i,j\}$, and we assume no $d(i,i)$ type dyads.”
(S2) Regression and estimand, p. 566: “Consider a linear regression of $Y_{d(i,j)}$ on a $k$-length column vector of regressors $X_{d(i,j)}$ (which includes the constant): $$Y_{d(i,j)} = X'_{d(i,j)}\beta + \epsilon_{d(i,j)},$$ where $\beta$ is the slope that we would obtain if we could fit this model to the entire population, allowing for possible non-linearity in the true relationship between $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ and $X_{d(i,j)}$, and $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is the corresponding population residual.$^3$ To lighten notation, for the remainder of the discussion we use $d = d(i,j)$.” Footnote 3, p. 566: “If $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ is non-linear in $X_{d(i,j)}$, the population residual will itself vary in $X_{d(i,j)}$, which undermines inference that assumes that $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is independent of $X_{d(i,j)}$. The agnostic regression approach avoids such an assumption.”
(S3) Estimator, p. 566: “Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X_1 ... X_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$. The ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator is $$\hat\beta = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'Y,$$ with residual $e_d = Y_d - X'_d\hat\beta$.”
(S4) Dependence, boundedness and rank, p. 566: “Since the values of $Y_d$ and $X_d$ are determined by the characteristics of the units $i$ and $j$, $\epsilon_d$ and $\epsilon_{d'}$ for dyads containing either unit $i$ or $j$ are allowed to be correlated by construction. However, by random sampling of units, $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) = 0$ for all dyads that do not share a member. The number of pairwise dependencies between $i$ and $j$ for which $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) \ne 0$ is $O(N^3)$. Let the support for $X_d$ and $Y_d$ be bounded in a finite interval and assume the usual rank conditions on $\mathbf{X}$ (Chamberlain 1982; White 1984).”
(S5) Neighbouring dyads, p. 566 (repeated on p. 573): “$\mathcal{S}(d) = \{d' \ne d\} \cap \{d' : s(d) \cap s(d') \ne \emptyset\}$, the set of dyads other than $d$ that share a member from $d$.”
(S6) Repeated dyads, p. 567 (PDF p. 4): “Formally, suppose that for each dyad $d$ observations are indexed by $t = 1, ..., T(d)$, where the $T(d)$ values are fixed and finite. Let $(Y_{dt}, X'_{dt})$ represent the data for observation $t$ from dyad $d$, $$Y_d = \begin{pmatrix} Y_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ Y_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{and}\quad X_d = \begin{pmatrix} X'_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ X'_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix},$$ and $Y = (Y'_1 \ldots Y'_d \ldots Y'_D)'$ and $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 \ldots X'_d \ldots X'_D)'$, that is, the stacked $Y_d$ vectors and $X_d$ matrices, and let $\beta_r$ and $\hat\beta_r$ denote, respectively, the population slope and OLS estimator as defined above but now applied to the repeated dyads data.” In this case $X_d$ is a $T(d) \times k$ matrix and $e_d$, $\epsilon_d$ are $T(d)$-vectors.
(S7) Weighted observations, Appendix D, p. 575 (PDF p. 12): “Assume weighted directed dyad observations with weights finite and fixed; denote the weight for dyad $d$ as $w_d$. Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 ... X'_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$ and the matrix of weights as $\mathbf{W} = \mathrm{diag}\{w_1, \ldots, w_D\}$. Then, the weighted least squares estimator is $$\hat\beta_w = (\mathbf{X}'WX)^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}Y.$$” (In the display the $W$ and $X$ inside the inverse are set in italic, not bold; the meaning is $(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X})^{-1}$.) The paper does not define $\beta_w$.
(S8) Simulation design, p. 569 (PDF p. 6): “We suppose that population values obey the following: $$Y_{d(i,j)t} = \beta_0 + \beta_1|X_i - X_j| + \underbrace{\alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}}_{\epsilon_{d(i,j)t}}, \qquad (4)$$ where $Y_{d(i,j)t}$ is the $t$th observed outcome for the dyad that includes units $i$ and $j$, $X_i$, $X_j$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_j$, and $u_{d(i,j)t}$ are independent draws from standard normal distributions, and the compound error, $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}$, is unobserved. In the cross-sectional case, we only observe one outcome per dyad, so $t = 1$ for all observations (i.e., the $t$ subscript is extraneous for the cross-sectional case). In the repeated observations case, we have two observations per dyad, so $t = 1, 2$ for all dyads. We fix $\beta_0 = 0$ and $\beta_1 = 1$. We use OLS to estimate $\hat\beta_0$ and $\hat\beta_1$.”
(S9) Reading used by the validators (the audit's formalization of S1–S4; not printed as such). Each unit carries a characteristic $U_i$, the $U_i$ are i.i.d., and $(X_{d(i,j)}, Y_{d(i,j)}) = f(U_i, U_j)$ for one symmetric measurable $f$, with $X_d \in \mathbb{R}^k$ and $Y_d \in \mathbb{R}$ bounded. Hence collections of dyads on disjoint sets of units are independent, and all dyads have the same marginal law. $Q = \mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]$ is nonsingular (the ‘usual rank conditions’), $\beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ is the population least-squares projection, $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta$, so that $\mathrm{E}[X_d\epsilon_d] = 0$; nothing makes $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}] = 0$. The limit is $N \to \infty$. For repeated dyads the reading is $\beta_r = (\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d])^{-1}\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X_d\beta_r$; for weights, $\beta_w = (\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d])^{-1}\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta_w$.
Scope of the list. Targets are the paper's formal results (Lemma 1, Propositions 1–2, Corollaries 1–2, the logistic estimator of Appendix E) and every confirmed error whose correction changes a mathematical statement, a formula or a proof step: P018-E001, E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E007, N001, N003, N004, N006, N010. Two findings about the reported evidence rest on exact formal arguments and are targets for that formal content only: P018-E008 (the fitted random-effects benchmark has a covariance family that excludes the covariance of design (4)) and P018-E012 (‘an order of magnitude’ against the ratios of Table 1; the validator's evidence is itself a Lean proof). Not targets: P018-E009 (a mislabelled curve in SI Figure 4), E010 (sample counts), E011 (description of a regressor), E014 and E015 (wording and reference-list misprints), N008 (a cross-reference), which are findings about figures, data, reporting and bibliography with no mathematical statement to correct; P018-E013 and N002 (clarity notes); P018-N005 and N009 (not confirmed); P018-N007, N011, N012, N013 (out of scope). Of the headline claims, P018-H1 (Lemma 1, Proposition 1), H3 (Corollaries 1–2), H4 (Appendix E) and H5 (Proposition 2) are mathematical statements and are covered by P018-T26–T29, T14 and T16; H2 is the interpretive claim of valid inference under misspecification, whose formal content is T2, T4 and T8; H6–H10 are simulation and empirical claims.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Corollaries 1 and 2, first conclusion, corrected: $V_r$ and $V_w$ are the covariances of the asymptotic linear approximation (and of the limiting distribution); the conclusion kept is $N\hat V - V \overset{p}{\to} 0$; convergence of the finite-sample variance needs uniform integrability
canonical_claim.location: p. 567 (PDF p. 4), Corollary 1; p. 575 (PDF p. 12), Corollary 2
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed: Corollary 1, “Then, as $N\to\infty$, $$N\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta_r - \beta_r] - V_r\overset{p}{\to}0,$$ and $$N\hat V_r - V_r\overset{p}{\to}0,$$” and Corollary 2, “Then, as $N\to\infty$, $$N\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta_w - \beta_w] - V_w\overset{p}{\to}0,$$ and $$N\hat V_w - V_w\overset{p}{\to}0,$$”.
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-N004), verbatim: “Remove the first actual finite-sample variance conclusions of Corollaries 1 and 2 and describe V_r and V_w as covariances of the asymptotic linear approximations/distributional limits. Retain the in-probability sandwich conclusions with a proof based on normalized bounded score sums and inverse-Gram convergence in probability, replacing Appendix B's assertions about moments of the full sandwich. To retain the stronger actual covariance conclusions instead, impose and verify uniform integrability of N times the squared coefficient error; corresponding full-estimator moment control is also required for Appendix B's moment proof.”
Corrected statement, with every hypothesis.
(i) [What $V_r$ and $V_w$ are] Under the setting and definitions of P018-T12, for every $N$: $V_r = \mathrm{Var}\big(H_r^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{L}\sum_dX'_d\epsilon_d\big)$ and $V_w = \mathrm{Var}\big(H_w^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{D}\sum_dw_dX_d\epsilon_d\big)$: the exact covariance of the linear approximation to $\sqrt N(\hat\beta - \beta)$ obtained by replacing the sample Gram matrix by its expectation. These are finite for bounded data.
(ii) [Conclusion kept] Under the hypotheses of P018-T10: $N\hat V_r - V_r\overset{p}{\to}0$ and $N\hat V_w - V_w\overset{p}{\to}0$. The first printed conclusion of each corollary is removed: under the stated conditions $\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta_r - \beta_r]$ and $\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta_w - \beta_w]$ need not be finite for any $N$ (P018-T19).
(iii) [Sufficient condition for the removed conclusion] Let $\xi_N = \sqrt N(\hat\beta - \beta)$. If $\xi_N\Rightarrow\xi$ with $\mathrm{E}[\xi] = 0$, $\mathrm{Var}(\xi) = V_\infty$, and $\{\|\xi_N\|^2\}_N$ is uniformly integrable, then $\mathrm{E}[\xi_N]\to0$ and $N\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta - \beta] = \mathrm{Var}(\xi_N)\to V_\infty$; if moreover the target of (i) converges to $V_\infty$, then $N\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta - \beta] - V\to0$. Boundedness of the data together with sample and population rank conditions does not imply this uniform integrability (P018-T19).
(iv) [Notation] $N\mathrm{Var}[\hat\beta - \beta] - V$ is a deterministic sequence, so ‘$\overset{p}{\to}0$’ in the first printed conclusion can only mean ‘$\to0$’.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Corollaries as printed: P018-T28, P018-T29. Corrected targets $V_r$, $V_w$ and $H_r$, $H_w$, $L$: P018-T12. Hypotheses for (ii): P018-T10. The same correction applies to the proof of Proposition 1: Appendix B's conditions on $\mathrm{E}[\hat V]$ and $\mathrm{Var}[N\hat V]$ are replaced by the probability-limit argument of P018-T4.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (i) is exact for every $N$ (from the linearization identities of P018-T12 (i)). (iii) is the standard fact that convergence in distribution with uniformly integrable squares gives convergence of first and second moments.
canonical_claim.note: Corrected statement for P018-N004 (error, Minor). Repair cost per the validator: weaker conclusion (the claim about the actual finite-sample variance is dropped) or a substantive additional tail condition, which the validator did not establish for the paper's applications. In the model of P018-T19 the limiting covariance exists, is positive definite and is consistently estimated by $N\hat V_r$, so the kept conclusion holds there.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Lemma 1, equation (2), term $B$: the expectation operator printed inside the summation subscript, corrected to stand before the braces as in equation (6)
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed (p. 566, term $B$ of (2)): $$\underbrace{\sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)\,\mathrm{E}}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\}}_{B}$$ with the letter $\mathrm{E}$ set on the baseline of the summation subscript, after ‘$d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)$’.
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-N001), verbatim: “$\sum_{d^{\prime}\in\mathcal S(d)}\mathrm E\{X_dX_{d^{\prime}}^{\prime}\operatorname{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d^{\prime}}\mid\mathbf X]\}$.”
Formal content of the corrected notation (the audit's unfolding; the misprint is typographic). For each dyad $d$ put $A_d = \mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_d\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]\}$ and $$B_d = \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\},$$ a finite sum of $k\times k$ matrices of expectations. Then, for $N \ge 2$:
(i) $|\mathcal{S}(d)| = 2(N-2)$ for every dyad $d$, so term $B$ has $2(N-2)$ summands for each $d$ and $\sum_d|\mathcal{S}(d)| = N(N-1)(N-2)$.
(ii) $$\sum_{d=1}^{D}(A_d + B_d) = \sum_{(d,d'):\,s(d)\cap s(d')\ne\emptyset}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\},$$ the sum on the right being over the $D(2N-3)$ ordered pairs of dyads that are equal or share a member. So with the operator placed before the braces the right-hand side of (2) is, term for term, the third line of (6), and it is the second line of (6) restricted to the pairs with $s(d)\cap s(d')\ne\emptyset$.
(iii) This correction does not make equation (2) true: the corrected identity for $\mathrm{Var}[\sum_dX_d\epsilon_d]$ is P018-T2 (ii), with $\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_{d'}\epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}]$ in place of $\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\}$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Equation (2) in full, as printed: P018-T26. Equation (6): P018-T1. $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5). $A_d$ and $B_d$ are this audit's names for the paper's underbraced terms $A$ and $B$ at a given $d$.
canonical_claim.note: P018-N001 is rated an error, Minor: a misplaced symbol in a formula, with the intended placement fixed by equation (6). Included on the author's instruction that every confirmed mathematical error, at any severity, has a corrected-statement target. The correction alone leaves a false identity (P018-E001), which is why the formal content is confined to the counting statements (i)–(ii) and (iii) points to P018-T2. Validation was a page check in the batch; there is no derivation beyond it.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 4, the list of independent draws below equation (4), corrected ($\nu_{d(i,j)t}$ for the printed $u_{d(i,j)t}$), with the covariance of the compound error that the corrected design implies
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed: “where $Y_{d(i,j)t}$ is the $t$th observed outcome for the dyad that includes units $i$ and $j$, $X_i$, $X_j$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_j$, and $u_{d(i,j)t}$ are independent draws from standard normal distributions, and the compound error, $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + 
u_{d(i,j)t}$, is unobserved.”
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-N006), verbatim: “Replace $u_{d(i,j)t}$ by $
u_{d(i,j)t}$.”
Corrected: “[...] $X_i$, $X_j$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_j$, and $
u_{d(i,j)t}$ are independent draws from standard normal distributions, and the compound error, $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + 
u_{d(i,j)t}$, is unobserved.”
Formal content of the corrected design (the audit's unfolding). Let $(X_i)_{i\le N}$, $(\alpha_i)_{i\le N}$ and $(
u_{dt})_{d\le D,\,t\le T}$ be mutually independent standard normal variables, and $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + 
u_{d(i,j)t}$. Then the $\epsilon_{dt}$ are jointly normal with mean zero, independent of $(X_i)_i$, and for dyads $d, d'$ and observations $t, t'$: $$\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_{dt},\epsilon_{d't'}) = |s(d)\cap s(d')| + \mathbf{1}\{d = d',\ t = t'\},$$ that is: 3 for the same observation, 2 for two observations of the same dyad, 1 for observations of distinct dyads that share a unit, and 0 for dyads with no unit in common. In particular $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_{dt}\,|\,X_1,\ldots,X_N] = 0$, so in this design $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)t}\,|\,X_i,X_j] =  eta_0 +  eta_1|X_i - X_j|$ and the linear regression of $Y$ on $(1, |X_i - X_j|)$ is correctly specified.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Equation (4) and its paragraph: (S8). $s(d)$: (S1). In the cross-sectional case $T = 1$; in the repeated case $T = 2$.
canonical_claim.note: P018-N006 is rated an error, Minor: a one-symbol misprint (Latin $u$ for Greek $\nu$) in the statement of the simulation design; no separate $u$ is defined. Included on the author's instruction that every confirmed mathematical error has a corrected-statement target. The covariance formula is the one both validators of P018-E008 use (P018-T5 (a)) and is given here for $T \ge 1$. Validation was a page check in the batch.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix E, the generic sandwich matrices and the logistic linear predictor, corrected: $\mathbf{B} = \mathrm{E}[\psi(D;\hat\theta)\psi(D;\hat\theta)']$ (printed with an undefined $D_i$) and $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(X'_d\hat\beta)$ (printed without the transpose)
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed: “Given an estimating equation, $\psi(D;\theta)$, on data $D$, and with parameters $\theta$ and parameter estimates $\hat\theta$, the sandwich approximation for the variance is $\mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{B}\{\mathbf{A}^{-1}\}'$, where $$\mathbf{A} = \mathrm{E}\Big[-\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta'}\psi(D;\hat\theta)\Big] \text{ and } \mathbf{B} = \mathrm{E}\,\psi(D;\hat\theta)\psi(D_i;\hat\theta)'.$$ For logistic regression, the estimating equation is $$\psi((\mathbf{X}_d, Y_d);\hat\beta) = \mathbf{X}_d(Y_d - p_d),$$ where $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(\mathbf{X}_d\hat\beta)$, the predicted probability for dyad $d$.”
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-N010), verbatim: “$\mathbf B=\mathrm E[\psi(D;\hat\theta)\psi(D;\hat\theta)^{\prime}]$ and $p_d=\operatorname{expit}(X_d^{\prime}\hat\beta)$. Optionally rename the locally defined data argument to avoid overloading D.”
Formal content of the corrected formulas, with every hypothesis. Let $k \ge 1$, $\mathrm{expit}(t) = 1/(1+e^{-t})$, and for $x\in\mathbb{R}^k$, $y\in\mathbb{R}$, $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^k$ let $\psi((x,y);\beta) = x\,(y - \mathrm{expit}(x'\beta))\in\mathbb{R}^k$. Then:
(i) $x'\beta$ is a scalar, so $\mathrm{expit}(x'\beta)\in(0,1)$ is defined; for column vectors $x, \beta\in\mathbb{R}^k$ with $k > 1$ the printed product $x\beta$ is not conformable.
(ii) $\psi((x,y);\beta)$ is the gradient in $\beta$ of $y\,x'\beta - \log(1 + e^{x'\beta})$ (the Bernoulli log-likelihood of one observation when $y\in\{0,1\}$).
(iii) $-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial\beta'}\psi((x,y);\beta) = p(1-p)\,xx'$ with $p = \mathrm{expit}(x'\beta)$: a symmetric positive semidefinite $k\times k$ matrix that does not depend on $y$.
(iv) $\psi((x,y);\beta)\psi((x,y);\beta)' = xx'(y - p)^2$, a $k\times k$ matrix of the same dimension as (iii).
(v) For data $(X_d, Y_d)_{d\le D}$ and any $\hat\beta$, with $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(X'_d\hat\beta)$, $r_d = Y_d - p_d$ and $\mathbf{M} = \mathrm{diag}(p_d(1-p_d))$: $$\sum_{d=1}^{D}-\frac{\partial}{\partial\beta'}\psi((X_d,Y_d);\hat\beta) = \mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \sum_{d=1}^{D}\psi((X_d,Y_d);\hat\beta)\psi((X_d,Y_d);\hat\beta)' = \sum_{d=1}^{D}X_dX'_dr_d^2,$$ the bread of $\hat V_l$ and the diagonal part of its middle factor (P018-T14).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: $\hat V_l$, $\mathbf{M}$ and $r_d$ as printed: P018-T13; corrected $\hat V_l$: P018-T14. $X_d$ is the $k$-length column vector of (S2) (printed in bold in Appendix E and in italic elsewhere). The paper does not define expit. In Appendix E the letter $D$ is locally the data argument of $\psi$, elsewhere the number of dyads; the validator does not count this reuse as an error.
canonical_claim.note: P018-N010 is rated an error, Minor (confirmed in part): two misprints in formulas whose intended forms are plain; the reuse of $D$ was not upheld as an error. Included on the author's instruction that every confirmed mathematical error has a corrected-statement target. (ii)–(v) are the facts that the fresh readers checked and that the audit records as holding (‘the logistic score $X_d(Y_d - p_d)$ and Hessian $X'\,\mathrm{diag}(p_d(1-p_d))\,X$ are correct’). The cross term of $\hat V_l$ is the separate finding P018-E005 (P018-T13, P018-T14).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 5, ‘standard error estimates that are sometimes an order of magnitude larger than what we obtain when we ignore all clustering’, corrected against Table 1: the ratios of column (6) to column (4) are between about 2.3 and 4.4, and none can reach 10 whatever the rounding
canonical_claim.location: p. 571 (PDF p. 8), Section 5, second paragraph; Table 1, p. 572 (PDF p. 9)
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed (p. 571): “Accounting for the dyadic and repeated-observation clustering results in standard error estimates that are sometimes an order of magnitude larger than what we obtain when we ignore all clustering and also considerably larger than what one would estimate were one to account for repeated dyads clustering but ignore the inter-dyadic clustering.”
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-E012), verbatim: “Replace 'sometimes an order of magnitude larger' with 'several times as large'. For a precise displayed-table description, say 'about 2.3 to 4.4 times as large as the displayed estimates that ignore all clustering'.”
Data (Table 1, p. 572, rows Alliances, Power ratio, Lower democracy, Lower dependence, International organizations, Non-contiguity, Log distance, Only minor powers, Constant). Column (4) ‘Het. Robust S.E.’, $H$: 0.069, 0.020, 0.005, 10.734, 0.002, 0.074, 0.026, 0.078, 0.211. Column (5) ‘Naive cluster Robust S.E.’, $C$: 0.175, 0.047, 0.010, 17.560, 0.005, 0.181, 0.068, 0.188, 0.562. Column (6) ‘Dyadic cluster Robust S.E.’, $D$: 0.265, 0.070, 0.015, 24.749, 0.008, 0.185, 0.102, 0.344, 0.840. Column (3) coefficient for International organizations: $-0.011$.
Formal content (exact rational arithmetic on the printed decimals).
(i) The nine ratios $D/H$ are $\tfrac{265}{69}, \tfrac72, 3, \tfrac{24749}{10734}, 4, \tfrac52, \tfrac{51}{13}, \tfrac{172}{39}, \tfrac{840}{211}$; the smallest is $\tfrac{24749}{10734}$ (Lower dependence, about 2.31) and the largest $\tfrac{172}{39}$ (Only minor powers, about 4.41). Every ratio is below 5, hence below 10.
(ii) [Rounding cannot hide a tenfold ratio] With $e = \tfrac1{2000}$: in each row $H - e > 0$ and $D + e < 10(H - e)$. Hence for all real $h, d$ with $H - e\le h$ and $d\le D + e$ (in particular all values that round to the printed three decimals), $d/h < 10$. The row-wise upper bounds $(D+e)/(H-e)$ are $\tfrac{531}{137}, \tfrac{47}{13}, \tfrac{31}{9}, \tfrac{49499}{21467}, \tfrac{17}{3}, \tfrac{53}{21}, \tfrac{205}{51}, \tfrac{689}{155}, \tfrac{1681}{421}$, each at most $\tfrac{17}{3}$.
(iii) [The direction of both comparisons is correct] In every row $D > C > H$; the ratios $D/C$ range from $\tfrac{185}{181}$ (Non-contiguity) to $\tfrac{86}{47}$ (Only minor powers).
(iv) [The significance statement survives] For International organizations, $\tfrac{0.011}{0.008} = \tfrac{11}{8} < 1.64$; for all reals with $|b|\le\tfrac{23}{2000}$ and $se\ge\tfrac{15}{2000}$, $|b|/se\le\tfrac{23}{15} < \tfrac{41}{25} = 1.64$; and with the heteroskedasticity-robust standard error, $|b|\ge\tfrac{21}{2000}$, $0 < se$ and $se\le\tfrac{5}{2000}$ give $|b|/se\ge\tfrac{21}{5} > 1.64$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: p. 571: “Column (4) contains estimates that account only for dyad-year heteroskedasticity, Column (5) also accounts for arbitrary dependence over time for each dyad, and then Column (6) also accounts for dyadic clustering.” So ‘ignore all clustering’ is column (4) and the comparison is column (6) over column (4); the table labels all three columns ‘S.E.’ (standard errors, not variances). ‘An order of magnitude larger’ is read as a factor of about ten. p. 571: “the coefficient for international organizations would fail to pass a conventional significance test (e.g., $t > 1.64$).” The table values above were read from the page image of p. 572.
canonical_claim.note: P018-E012 is rated an error, Minor: an overstated magnitude in the prose; the table beside the sentence gives the true magnitudes. It is a finding about reporting and is a target only because it rests on exact arithmetic: the validator's evidence is itself a Lean proof of (i), (ii) and (iv) (check.lean in the artifact, compiled with no sorry). The formalizer may reuse or restate it. The validator's reconstruction from the authors' data gives an unrounded largest ratio of about 4.68 (HC0), on a sample that differs from the table note (P018-E010); that reconstruction is empirical and is not part of the target.
